output.brief: The volunteer drop is not mainly about the app itself, the background checks, or Commonplate. It comes from two changes acting together. RotaWeave's basic tier keeps no standing weekly slots. A regular keeps a slot only if staff book it before the Thursday release. Until 1 May, coordinators did that booking. At Dock Street and Westgate the coordinator posts were cut that day, and bookings on behalf of volunteers fell from 74 a week to 3. About 129 of 213 regulars lost their usual slot at least twice, and 88% of them are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept it. Millbrook has the app and a coordinator, and its numbers are stable. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app and a paper roster, and it is also stable. The background-check deadline hit all sites equally, and 21 of the 23 deactivated volunteers came back. 121 of the 123 who lapsed had a current check, so renewal isn't the cause. Only 2 of the 61 people reached by callback said they had joined another group. Don't cancel RotaWeave, suspend the checks or purge the rolls. Instead, assign someone to book regulars into their usual slots before each release at Dock Street and Westgate, and phone lapsed volunteers to offer their slot back. I'm fairly confident in this. The main gap is that the evidence is observational.
